verifier: adversarial verifier, integ2 engine round 1 (2026-10-29). Re-measured at HEAD c015bf50; the lane's files are clean in the working tree and pushed. I did not trust the engineers' reports.
summary: Lane engine fails round 1 on one regression from engine-lod. The crowd LOD now simplifies the Wicks' team-colour accent parts, so the shieldwick hood stripe breaks into dashes and the greatwick's hood band mostly disappears at the gameplay camera. engine-lod's own gates reproduce. perf_1080 --prod GATE PASS: match peak 451,815 tris at 1309.9 s, 40 programs (exactly at the cap), 273 draws, 0 seconds over budget, 0 programs first seen after 1:00, High 249k / Low 171k, memory +0.6 %, dynres PASS. Fighter LOD1 is clean for all 16 fighters at the gameplay camera, with faces locked and the menu drawing full bodies. The engineers' own probe left Tunlan and Kemdo as empty crops, so I added two more runs with picks. The crowd regression is new in this round. In run 1, lodIndex skipped meshes under 600 triangles, so the accent parts (98-332 tris) were drawn whole. crowd.ts now gives every part LOD.crowd (0.25 within 12 mm, minTrisCrowd 96). I ran an in-page A/B in the bench at RIFT t 900 seed 7. Shieldwick accent pixels go 608 -> 445 (-27 %) and the greatwick's 604 -> 442. Keeping only the accent parts whole, with the body and hull LOD unchanged, restores them (653 / 617). probe_lod still passes (frame mean 0.14, 0.115 % of pixels > 24 levels), because its whole-frame gate is too coarse to see it. Minor items: engine-r2-06 and all four pkg2 items pass. Negative scratch-copy tests raised errors for an unknown fighterWeights key, a wrong bansPerTeam, an unknown ambience cue and an unknown ambience map key. A shipped-content copy-lint hit is still an error, and COPY_LINT_PENDING is empty. engine-r2-01 and engine-r2-02 are partly. All 9 new VFX defs exist; they were merged additively (272 -> 281, 0 existing defs changed) and the generator reproduces each one exactly. Wiring content to them is a systems handoff, and every JSON path in it checks out. Two design nits: ervet_ult_shards_home keeps a 3.3-3.4x 'blade' mesh described as 'the oversized blade', which the W4 re-key cut (_design/fighters/ervet.md:30), and vashil_passive_chord has no line joining the two humming enemies. The optional items engine-r2-03, -04 and -05 were skipped. combat:F4 is not done, as the engineers said. Box white is <= 0.35 for all four (Kemdo 0.024, Rishal 0.17, Tunlan 0.199, Hesmi 0.279), but the probe exits 1 on core ratio (Tunlan 2.06, Hesmi 2.21). value_probe RIFT Low flash is 1.94x (High 2.11x). These numbers equal run 1's, so nothing got worse. Other checks are clean: typecheck 0, content:check 0 warnings, probe_content_build 126/126, probe_content_ids, probe_maps, probe_render_dynres(+vsync), probe_camera_edge, secret scan PASS, npm run build OK, and RIFT value_probe matches run 1 on every gate. I A/B'd the landmark white texel in the bench and it changes 0 pixels. Sensitivity: I viewed every new VFX sheet and every LOD shot. The LOD adds or removes no facial features, the Wicks stay faceless, and there are no new hoods or masks.

Its 'no difference' therefore covered 8 of 10, and 6 fighters were never in its match. I re-ran a scratch copy of probe_body_lod with --picks and actor visibility. Run p1 (ardit, ilsheta, lisvel, nurrow, sukri, ulkro, kemdo, rishal, vashil visible): _harness/_reports/integ2_engine_v1_p1_body_lod.{log,json}. Run p2 (tunlan as seat 0, plus odrum, burdam, marund, hesmi, ervet, ilsheta, sukri): integ2_engine_v1_p2_body_lod.{log,json}. Shots: _harness/_shots/integ2_engine_v1_p{1,2}_bodylod_*.png. All 16 base fighters draw vale_body_lod1 in the match. Bodies: 197,717 -> 107,844 (p1) and 192,387 -> 106,975 (p2). Tunlan goes 20,926 -> 8,405 and Ilsheta 17,004 -> 7,736, the most aggressive cuts. I compared every A|B pair at 2-6x. The faces are identical, as are Tunlan's hat mark, Sukri's face and Ervet's blade. The silhouettes differ only at edge pixels, and nothing pops (the LOD never switches mid-match). Menu: 0 LOD1 bodies.

CROWD REGRESSION (see regressions). Scratch in-page A/B on the dev server, RIFT t 900 seed 7, the probe_lod frame. Shots: _harness/_shots/integ2_engine_v1_crowdab_{full,lod,bodyOnly,accentOnly,hullOnly}.png and integ2_engine_v1_accent_{full,run2,accentFull}.png. The accent parts' LOD alone (accentOnly) erases the greatwick's orange hood band; body-only LOD keeps it. Accent pixels in the crops, full / shipped / accent kept whole: shieldwick blue 608 / 445 / 653, greatwick orange 604 / 442 / 617, glimwick orange 2173 / 2151 / 2203. Index counts show every accent part between 98 and 332 tris is now simplified (708 -> 264, 996 -> 348, 750 -> 183, 660 -> 165, 294 -> 72). In run 1 they were drawn whole: 8faff08c lod.ts `if (count / 3 < minTris ...) return null` with minTris 600. probe_lod: `node _harness/probe_lod.mjs --no-build --out _harness/_reports/integ2_engine_v1_lod.json` PASS (mean 0.14, over24 0.115 %, shadow share 0.20), but that gate is too coarse to catch this.
items.fixHint: src/render/crowd.ts bakeCrowd: draw the accent parts whole, as run 1 did: `const lods = meshes.map((m, i) => (m.material as Material).name === accentName ? null : lodIndex(m.geometry, 'crowd', LOD.minTrisCrowd, units[i]));`. composeIndex then keeps the accent members' own triangles in the hull, which costs about 150-250 tris per unit. Alternatively, lock the accent part's boundary and use a bound of 3 mm or less. Re-check with the in-page accent A/B: accent pixels within 3 % of full for shieldwick, greatwick and glimwick at RIFT t 900 seed 7. Then run one perf_1080 --prod match peak, which must stay <= 500k and <= 40 programs. Separately, make probe_body_lod fail on an invisible actor (actor root not visible, or 'fighters main' 0) instead of reporting crop mean 0 as 'no difference', and add a --picks pass-through so all 16 fighters can be covered.
